modelEssay.title: The Importance of Building Trust Between Employers and Employees
modelEssay.content:
Trust forms the cornerstone of any successful business relationship. In the workplace, fostering trust between employers and employees is crucial for a harmonious and productive environment.

Firstly, trust enhances job satisfaction and loyalty. When employees trust their employers, they are more likely to feel valued and motivated, leading to increased productivity. For instance, a study by the Harvard Business Review found that companies with high trust levels outperformed their peers by 286%. Moreover, trust can reduce turnover rates as employees are less likely to leave a company where they feel trusted and respected.

In conclusion, building trust between employers and employees is not just a nice-to-have; it's a must-have for any organization aiming for success. It can lead to increased productivity, reduced costs, and a more positive work culture.

transcript.text: Passage 1.
transcript.translation: 段落1。

transcript.text: Many people enjoy secret codes.
transcript.translation: 许多人喜欢密码。

transcript.text: The harder the code, the more some people will try to figure it out.
transcript.translation: 密码越难，有些人就越想破解它。

transcript.text: In wartime, codes are especially important.
transcript.translation: 在战时，密码尤为重要。

transcript.text: They help armies send news about battles and the size of enemy forces.
transcript.translation: 它们帮助军队传递关于战斗和敌军规模的消息。

transcript.text: Neither side wants its code broken by the other.
transcript.translation: 任何一方都不希望己方密码被对方破解。

transcript.text: One very important code was never broken.
transcript.translation: 有一个非常重要的密码从未被破解。

transcript.text: It was used during World War II by the Americans.
transcript.translation: 它在第二次世界大战期间被美国人使用。

transcript.text: It was a spoken code, never written down.
transcript.translation: 它是一种口头密码，从未被记录下来。

transcript.text: And it was developed and used by Navajo Indians.
transcript.translation: 并且它是由纳瓦霍印第安人开发和使用的。

transcript.text: They were called the Navajo Code Talkers.
transcript.translation: 他们被称为纳瓦霍密码通信兵。

transcript.text: The Navajos created the code in their own language.
transcript.translation: 纳瓦霍人用自己的语言创造了这种密码。

transcript.text: Navajo is hard to learn, and only a few people know it.
transcript.translation: 纳瓦霍语很难学，只有少数人会说。

transcript.text: So it was pretty certain that the enemy would not be able to understand the Code Talkers.
transcript.translation: 因此可以相当肯定，敌人无法理解密码通信兵的话。

transcript.text: In addition, the Talkers used code words.
transcript.translation: 此外，通信兵们还使用密码词。

transcript.text: They called a submarine an iron fish, and a small bomb thrown by hand a potato.
transcript.translation: 他们称潜艇为‘铁鱼’，称手掷的小炸弹为‘土豆’。

transcript.text: If they wanted to spell something, they used code words for letters of the alphabet.
transcript.translation: 如果想拼写什么，他们就用字母表的代码词。

transcript.text: For instance, the letter A was ant or apple or axe.
transcript.translation: 例如，字母A是‘蚂蚁’、‘苹果’或‘斧头’。

transcript.text: The Code Talkers worked mostly in the islands in the Pacific.
transcript.translation: 密码通信兵主要在太平洋的岛屿上工作。

transcript.text: One or two would be assigned to a group of soldiers.
transcript.translation: 一到两名会被分配到一个士兵小组。

transcript.text: They would send messages by field telephone to the Code Talker in the next group.
transcript.translation: 他们通过野战电话向下一组的密码通信兵发送消息。

transcript.text: And he would relay the information to his commander.
transcript.translation: 然后他再将信息转达给他的指挥官。

transcript.text: The Code Talkers played an important part in several battles.
transcript.translation: 密码通信兵在几场战斗中发挥了重要作用。

transcript.text: They helped troops coordinate their movements and attacks.
transcript.translation: 他们帮助部队协调行动和攻击。

transcript.text: After the war, the U.
transcript.translation: 战后，U.

transcript.text: S.
transcript.translation: S.

transcript.text: government honored them for what they had accomplished.
transcript.translation: 政府为他们的成就而表彰了他们。

transcript.text: Theirs was the most successful wartime code ever used.
transcript.translation: 他们的密码是有史以来最成功的战时密码。

transcript.text: If you are young and thinking about your career, you'll want to know where you can make a living.
transcript.translation: 如果你还年轻，正在考虑你的职业，你会想知道在哪里可以谋生。

transcript.text: Well, there's going to be a technological replacement of a lot of knowledge-intensive jobs in the next 20 years, particularly in the two largest sectors of the labor force with professional skills.
transcript.translation: 嗯，在未来20年内，许多知识密集型工作将被技术取代，尤其是在劳动力中拥有专业技能的两个最大领域。

transcript.text: One is teaching, and the other, health care.
transcript.translation: 一个是教学，另一个是医疗保健。

transcript.text: You have so many applications and software and platforms that are going to come in and provide information and service in these two fields.
transcript.translation: 会有如此多的应用程序、软件和平台进入这两个领域，提供信息和服务。

transcript.text: Which means a lot of health care and education sectors will be radically changed, and a lot of jobs will be lost.
transcript.translation: 这意味着许多医疗保健和教育部门将发生根本性变化，许多工作岗位将会丧失。

transcript.text: Now, where will the new jobs be found?
transcript.translation: 那么，新的工作岗位将在哪里找到？

transcript.text: Well, the one sector of the economy that can't be easily duplicated by even smart technologies is the caring sector, the personal care sector.
transcript.translation: 嗯，经济中一个即使智能技术也难以轻易复制的领域是关怀行业，即个人护理行业。

transcript.text: That is, you can't really get a robot to do a great massage or physical therapy, or you can't get the kind of personal attention you need with regard to therapy or any other personal service.
transcript.translation: 也就是说，你无法真正让机器人进行出色的按摩或物理治疗，或者无法在治疗或其他任何个人服务方面获得你需要的那种个人关注。

transcript.text: There could be very high-end personal services.
transcript.translation: 可能会有非常高端的个人服务。

transcript.text: Therapists do charge a lot of money.
transcript.translation: 治疗师确实收费很高。

transcript.text: I think there's no limit to the amount of personal attention and personal care people would like if they could afford it.
transcript.translation: 我认为，如果人们负担得起，他们对个人关注和护理的需求是没有上限的。

transcript.text: But the real question in the future is, how can people afford these things if they don't have money, because they can't get a job that pays enough?
transcript.translation: 但未来的真正问题是，如果人们没有钱，因为他们找不到薪水足够高的工作，他们如何负担得起这些东西？

transcript.text: That's why I wrote this book, which is about how to reorganize the economy for the future when technology brings about disruptive changes to what we used to consider high-income work.
transcript.translation: 这就是我写这本书的原因，它探讨了当技术对我们过去认为的高收入工作带来颠覆性变化时，如何为未来重组经济。

transcript.text: American researchers have discovered the world's oldest paved road, a 4,600-year-old highway.
transcript.translation: 美国研究人员发现了世界上最古老的铺砌道路，一条有4600年历史的公路。

transcript.text: It linked a stone pit in the Egyptian desert to waterways that carried blocks to monument sites along the Nile.
transcript.translation: 它连接了埃及沙漠中的一个采石场和水道，这些水道将石块运送到尼罗河沿岸的纪念碑遗址。

transcript.text: The eight-mile road is at least 500 years older than any previously discovered road.
transcript.translation: 这条八英里长的道路比任何以前发现的道路至少早500年。

transcript.text: It is the only paved road discovered in ancient Egypt, said geologist Thomas Bowne of the United States Geological Survey.
transcript.translation: 这是在古埃及发现的唯一铺砌道路，美国地质调查局的地质学家托马斯·鲍恩说。

transcript.text: He reported the discovery on Friday.
transcript.translation: 他在周五报告了这一发现。

transcript.text: The road probably doesn't rank with the pyramids as a construction feat, but it is a major engineering achievement, said his colleague, geologist James Harrell of the University of Toledo.
transcript.translation: 这条道路可能无法与金字塔的建筑壮举相提并论，但它是一项重大的工程成就，他的同事、托莱多大学的地质学家詹姆斯·哈雷尔说。

transcript.text: Not only is the road earlier than we thought possible, we didn't even think they built roads.
transcript.translation: 不仅这条道路比我们想象的要早，我们甚至没想过他们建造了道路。

transcript.text: The researchers also made a discovery in the stone pit at the northern end of the road, the first evidence that the Egyptians used rock saws.
transcript.translation: 研究人员还在道路北端的采石场有了一个发现，这是埃及人使用岩石锯的首个证据。

transcript.text: This is the oldest example of saws being used for cutting stone, said Bowne's colleague James Hoffmeyer of Wheaton College in Illinois.
transcript.translation: 这是使用锯子切割石头的最古老例子，鲍恩的同事、伊利诺伊州惠顿学院的詹姆斯·霍夫迈耶说。

transcript.text: That's two technologies we didn't know they had, Harrell said.
transcript.translation: 这是我们不知道他们拥有的两项技术，哈雷尔说。

transcript.text: And we don't know why they were both abandoned.
transcript.translation: 而且我们不知道为什么这两项技术都被放弃了。

transcript.text: The road was discovered in the Fayum Depression, about 45 miles southwest of Cairo.
transcript.translation: 这条道路是在法尤姆洼地发现的，大约在开罗西南45英里处。

transcript.text: Short segments of the road had been observed by earlier explorers, Bowne said, but they failed to realise its significance or follow up on their observations.
transcript.translation: 早期的探险家观察到了这条道路的短段，鲍恩说，但他们没有意识到它的重要性，也没有跟进他们的观察。

transcript.text: Bowne and his colleague stumbled across it while they were doing geological mapping in the region.
transcript.translation: 鲍恩和他的同事在该地区进行地质测绘时偶然发现了它。

transcript.text: The road was clearly built to provide services for the newly discovered stone pit.
transcript.translation: 这条道路显然是为了新发现的采石场提供服务而建造的。

transcript.text: Bowne and Harrell have found the camp that housed workers at the stone pit.
transcript.translation: 鲍恩和哈雷尔已经找到了安置采石场工人的营地。

transcript.text: The road appears today to go nowhere, ending in the middle of the desert.
transcript.translation: 今天看来，这条道路似乎无处可去，终止于沙漠中央。

transcript.text: When it was built, its terminal was a dock on the shore of Lake Moiris, which had an elevation of about 66 feet above sea level, the same as the dock.
transcript.translation: 当它建成时，它的终点是莫里斯湖岸上的一个码头，海拔约66英尺，与码头相同。

transcript.text: Lake Moiris received its water from the annual floods of the Nile.
transcript.translation: 莫里斯湖的水来自尼罗河的年度洪水。

transcript.text: At the time of the floods, the river and lake were at the same level and connected through a gap in the hills, near the modern villages of El Lajun and Hawara.
transcript.translation: 在洪水期间，河流和湖泊处于同一水位，并通过山中的一个缺口相连，靠近现代村庄El Lajun和Hawara。

transcript.text: Harrell and Bowne believe that blocks were loaded onto barges during the dry season, then floated over to the Nile during the floods to be shipped off to the monument sites at Giza and Saqqara.
transcript.translation: 哈雷尔和鲍恩认为，在旱季，石块被装上驳船，然后在洪水期间漂浮到尼罗河，再运送到吉萨和萨卡拉的纪念碑遗址。

transcript.text: Dr.

transcript.translation: 龚医生将它们刺入我的左臂，在一直困扰我的肘部周围。

transcript.text: Other needles were slipped into my left wrist and, strangely, into my right arm, and then into both my closed eyelids.
transcript.translation: 其他针被滑入我的左腕，奇怪的是，还刺入了我的右臂，然后是我的两个闭着的眼皮。

transcript.text: There wasn't any discomfort, just a mild warming sensation.
transcript.translation: 没有任何不适，只有一种轻微的温暖感。

transcript.text: However, I did begin to wonder what had driven me here.
transcript.translation: 然而，我开始想知道是什么驱使我来到这里。

transcript.text: To the office of Dr.
transcript.translation: 来到医生的办公室。

transcript.text: James Gong in New York's Chinatown.
transcript.translation: 位于纽约唐人街的詹姆斯·龚医生的办公室。

transcript.text: Then I remembered the torturing pain in that left elbow.
transcript.translation: 然后我想起了左肘部那折磨人的疼痛。

transcript.text: Several trips to a hospital and two expensive, uncomfortable medical tests had failed to produce even a diagnosis.
transcript.translation: 几次去医院和两次昂贵且不舒服的医疗检查都没能给出一个诊断。

transcript.text: Maybe you lean on your left arm too much, the doctor concluded, suggesting I see a bone doctor.
transcript.translation: 也许你过于依赖左臂了，医生总结道，并建议我去看骨科医生。

transcript.text: During the hours spent waiting in vain to see a bone doctor, I decided to take another track and try acupuncture.
transcript.translation: 在徒劳等待骨科医生的几个小时里，我决定换条路，尝试针灸。

transcript.text: A Chinese-American friend recommended Dr.
transcript.translation: 一位华裔朋友推荐了医生。

transcript.text: Gong.

transcript.text: I took the subway to Gong's second floor office, marked with a hand-painted sign.
transcript.translation: 我乘地铁去龚医生的二楼办公室，那里有一个手绘的招牌。

transcript.text: Dr.

transcript.text: Gong speaks English, but not often.
transcript.translation: 龚医生说英语，但不经常。

transcript.text: Most of my questions to him were greeted with a friendly laugh, but I managed to let him know where my arm hurt.
transcript.translation: 我问他大多数问题时，他都报以友好的笑声，但我还是设法让他知道我的手臂哪里疼。

transcript.text: He asked me to go into a room, had me lie down on a bed, and went to work.
transcript.translation: 他让我进一个房间，让我躺在床上，然后开始工作。

transcript.text: In the next room, I learned a woman dancer was also getting a treatment.
transcript.translation: 在隔壁房间，我得知一位女舞者也在接受治疗。

transcript.text: As I lay there a while, I drifted into a dreamlike state and fantasized about what she looked like.
transcript.translation: 我在那里躺了一会儿，进入了一种梦幻般的状态，并幻想着她的模样。

transcript.text: Acupuncturists today are as likely to be found on Park Avenue as on Mott Street.

transcript.translation: 总计，全国估计有10,000名针灸师。

transcript.text: Acupuncturists may say that the body has more than 800 acupuncture points.
transcript.translation: 针灸师可能会说身体有800多个针灸点。

transcript.text: A life force called T circulates through the body.
transcript.translation: 一种称为T的生命力在体内循环。

transcript.text: Points on the skin are energetically connected to specific organs, body structures, and systems.
transcript.translation: 皮肤上的点与特定器官、身体结构和系统有能量上的联系。

transcript.text: Acupuncture points are stimulated to balance the circulation of T.
transcript.translation: 针灸点被刺激以平衡T的循环。

transcript.text: The truth is, though, acupuncture is at least 2,200 years old.

transcript.text: Nobody really knows what's happening, says Paul Zmiewski, a Ph.

transcript.text: Ronald and Lois, married for two decades, consider themselves a happy couple, but in the early years of their marriage, both were disturbed by persistent arguments that seemed to fade away without ever being truly resolved.
transcript.translation: 罗纳德和洛伊丝结婚二十年了，他们自认为是一对幸福的夫妇，但在婚姻的早年，他们都受到持续争吵的困扰，这些争吵似乎逐渐消失，但从未真正解决。

transcript.text: They uncovered clues to what was going wrong by researching a fascinating subject, how birth order affects not only your personality, but also how compatible you are with your mate.
transcript.translation: 他们通过研究一个迷人的主题——出生顺序如何不仅影响你的个性，还影响你与伴侣的相容性——揭开了问题所在的一些线索。

transcript.text: Ronald and Lois are only children, and onlys grow up accustomed to being the apple of their parents' eyes.
transcript.translation: 罗纳德和洛伊丝都是独生子女，独生子女在成长过程中习惯于成为父母的掌上明珠。

transcript.text: Match two onlys, and you have partners who subconsciously expect each other to continue fulfilling this expectation, while neither has much experience in the giving end.
transcript.translation: 将两个独生子女配对，你得到的是一对潜意识里期望对方继续满足这种期望的伴侣，而双方在付出方面都没有太多经验。

transcript.text: Here's a list of common birth order characteristics, and some thoughts on the best, and worst, marital matches for each.
transcript.translation: 以下是一些常见的出生顺序特征，以及对每种特征的最佳和最差婚姻匹配的一些思考。

transcript.text: The oldest tends to be self-assured, responsible, a high achiever, and relatively serious and reserved.
transcript.translation: 长子往往自信、负责、成就较高，并且相对严肃和矜持。

transcript.text: He may be slow to make friends, perhaps content with only one companion.
transcript.translation: 他可能交友较慢，或许满足于只有一个伴侣。

transcript.text: The best matches are with a youngest, an only, or a mate raised in a large family.
transcript.translation: 最佳匹配是与一个幼子、独生子女或在大家庭中长大的伴侣。

transcript.text: The worst match is with another oldest, since the two will be too sovereign to share a household comfortably.
transcript.translation: 最差匹配是与另一个长子，因为两人会过于独立，难以舒适地共享一个家庭。

transcript.text: The youngest child of the family thrives on attention, and tends to be outgoing, adventurous, optimistic, creative, and less ambitious than others in the family.
transcript.translation: 家庭中的幼子在关注中茁壮成长，往往外向、爱冒险、乐观、有创造力，并且比家庭中的其他人野心较小。

transcript.text: He may lack self-discipline, and have difficulty making decisions on his own.
transcript.translation: 他可能缺乏自律，在独自做决定方面有困难。

transcript.text: A youngest brother of brothers, often unpredictable and romantic, will match best with an oldest sister of brothers.
transcript.translation: 一个兄弟中的幼弟，往往不可预测且浪漫，最适合与兄弟中的长姐匹配。

transcript.text: The youngest sister of brothers is best matched with an oldest brother of sisters, who will happily indulge these traits.
transcript.translation: 兄弟中的幼妹最适合与姐妹中的长兄匹配，后者会乐于纵容这些特质。

transcript.text: The middle child is influenced by many variables, however, middles are less likely to take initiative, and more anxious and self-critical than others.
transcript.translation: 中间子女受许多变量影响，然而，中间子女不太可能主动，并且比其他人更焦虑和自我批评。

transcript.text: Middles often successfully marry other middles, since both are strong on tact, not so strong on aggressiveness, and tend to crave affection.
transcript.translation: 中间子女经常成功地与其他中间子女结婚，因为双方都擅长策略，不那么好斗，并且渴望感情。

transcript.text: The only child is often most comfortable when alone, but since an only tends to be a well-adjusted individual, she'll eventually learn to relate to any chosen spouse.
transcript.translation: 独生子女往往在独处时最舒适，但由于独生子女往往适应良好，她最终会学会与任何选择的配偶相处。

transcript.text: The male only child expects his wife to make life easier, without getting much in return.
transcript.translation: 男性独生子女期望妻子让生活更轻松，而自己付出不多。

transcript.text: He is sometimes best matched with a younger sister of brothers.
transcript.translation: 他有时最适合与兄弟中的幼妹匹配。

transcript.text: The female only child, who tends to be slightly more flexible, is well matched with an older man, who will indulge her tendency to test his love.
transcript.translation: 女性独生子女往往更灵活一些，与年长男性匹配良好，后者会纵容她测试他爱意的倾向。

transcript.text: Her worst match?
transcript.translation: 她最差的匹配？

transcript.text: Another only, of course.
transcript.translation: 当然是另一个独生子女。

material.title: Peer Pressure Has a Positive Side

paragraphs.text: Parents of teenagers often view their children's friends with something like suspicion. They worry that the adolescent peer group has the power to push its members into behavior that is foolish and even dangerous. Such wariness is well founded: statistics show, for example, that a teenage driver with a same-age passenger in the car is at higher risk of a fatal crash than an adolescent driving alone or with an adult.
paragraphs.translation: 青少年的父母常常以一种近乎怀疑的态度看待他们孩子的朋友。他们担心，青少年同伴群体有力量推动其成员做出愚蠢甚至危险的行为。这种谨慎是有根据的：例如，统计数据显示，车上有同龄乘客的青少年司机发生致命车祸的风险，比单独驾驶或与成年人同行的青少年更高。

paragraphs.text: In a 2005 study, psychologist Laurence Steinberg of Temple University and his co-author, psychologist Margo Gardner, then at Temple, divided 306 people into three age groups: young adolescents, with a mean age of 14; older adolescents, with a mean age of 19; and adults, aged 24 and older. Subjects played a computerized driving game in which the player must avoid crashing into a wall that materializes, without warning, on the roadway. Steinberg and Gardner randomly assigned some participants to play alone or with two same-age peers looking on.
paragraphs.translation: 在2005年的一项研究中，天普大学的心理学家劳伦斯·斯坦伯格及其合著者，当时也在天普大学的心理学家玛戈·加德纳，将306人分为三个年龄组：平均年龄14岁的青少年；平均年龄19岁的较年长青少年；以及24岁及以上的成年人。受试者玩一个计算机驾驶游戏，玩家必须避免撞上突然出现在道路上的墙壁。斯坦伯格和加德纳随机分配一些参与者单独玩游戏或由两名同龄同伴观看。

paragraphs.text: Older adolescents scored about 50 percent higher on an index of risky driving when their peers were in the room—and the driving of early adolescents was fully twice as reckless when other young teens were around. In contrast, adults behaved in similar ways regardless of whether they were on their own or observed by others. "The presence of peers makes adolescents and youth, but not adults, more likely to take risks," Steinberg and Gardner concluded.
paragraphs.translation: 当同伴在房间内时，较年长青少年的风险驾驶指数得分高出约50%——而当其他青少年在场时，早期青少年的驾驶行为鲁莽程度完全翻倍。相比之下，成年人的行为方式类似，无论他们是否独自一人或被他人观察。斯坦伯格和加德纳总结道：“同伴的存在使青少年和年轻人更可能冒险，但成年人则不然。”

paragraphs.text: Yet in the years following the publication of this study, Steinberg began to believe that this interpretation did not capture the whole picture. As he and other researchers examined the question of why teens were more apt to take risks in the company of other teenagers, they came to suspect that a crowd's influence need not always be negative. Now some experts are proposing that we should take advantage of the teen brain's keen sensitivity to the presence of friends and leverage it to improve education.
paragraphs.translation: 然而，在这项研究发表后的几年里，斯坦伯格开始认为这种解释没有涵盖全貌。当他和其他研究人员探讨为什么青少年在同伴陪伴下更易冒险时，他们开始怀疑群体的影响未必总是负面的。现在，一些专家提出，我们应该利用青少年大脑对朋友存在的敏锐敏感性，并借助它来改善教育。

paragraphs.text: In a 2011 study, Steinberg and his colleagues turned to functional MRI (磁共振) to investigate how the presence of peers affects the activity in the adolescent brain. They scanned the brains of 40 teens and adults who were playing a virtual driving game designed to test whether players would brake at a yellow light or speed on through the crossroad.
paragraphs.translation: 在2011年的一项研究中，斯坦伯格及其同事使用功能性磁共振成像（fMRI）来调查同伴的存在如何影响青少年大脑的活动。他们扫描了40名青少年和成年人的大脑，这些人正在玩一个旨在测试玩家在黄灯时是否刹车或加速通过十字路口的虚拟驾驶游戏。

paragraphs.text: The brains of teenagers, but not adults, showed greater activity in two regions associated with rewards when they were being observed by same-age peers than when alone. In other words, rewards are more intense for teens when they are with peers, which motivates them to pursue higher-risk experiences that might bring a big payoff (such as the thrill of just making the light before it turns red). But Steinberg suspected this tendency could also have its advantages. In his latest experiment, published online in August, Steinberg and his colleagues used a computerized version of a card game called the Iowa Gambling Task to investigate how the presence of peers affects the way young people gather and apply information.
paragraphs.translation: 当青少年被同龄同伴观察时，其大脑中与奖励相关的两个区域比独自一人时表现出更高的活动度，而成年人则没有。换句话说，当青少年与同伴在一起时，奖励对他们来说更强烈，这激励他们追求可能带来巨大回报的高风险体验（例如，在红灯前刚好通过路口的刺激感）。但斯坦伯格怀疑这种倾向也可能有其优势。在他最新的一项于8月在线发表的实验中，斯坦伯格及其同事使用一个名为爱荷华赌博任务的纸牌游戏计算机版本，来调查同伴的存在如何影响年轻人收集和应用信息的方式。

paragraphs.text: The results: Teens who played the Iowa Gambling Task under the eyes of fellow adolescents engaged in more exploratory behavior, learned faster from both positive and negative outcomes, and achieved better performance on the task than those who played in solitude. "What our study suggests is that teenagers learn more quickly and more effectively when their peers are present than when they're on their own," Steinberg says. And this finding could have important implications for how we think about educating adolescents.
paragraphs.translation: 结果：在同伴注视下玩爱荷华赌博任务的青少年表现出更多的探索行为，从正面和负面结果中学习得更快，并且在任务中取得比独自玩耍的青少年更好的成绩。斯坦伯格说：“我们的研究表明，当同伴在场时，青少年学习得更快、更有效，比他们独自一人时。”这一发现可能对我们如何思考青少年教育具有重要意义。

paragraphs.text: Matthew D. Lieberman, a social cognitive neuroscientist at the University of California, Los Angeles, and author of the 2013 book Social: Why Our Brains Are Wired to Connect, suspects that the human brain is especially adept at learning socially salient information. He points to a classic 2004 study in which psychologists at Dartmouth College and Harvard University used functional MRI to track brain activity in 17 young men as they listened to descriptions of people while concentrating on either socially relevant cues (for example, trying to form an impression of a person based on the description) or more socially neutral information (such as noting the order of details in the description). The descriptions were the same in each condition, but people could better remember these statements when given a social motivation.
paragraphs.translation: 加州大学洛杉矶分校的社会认知神经科学家马修·D·利伯曼，也是2013年《社交：为什么我们的大脑天生倾向连接》一书的作者，推测人类大脑尤其擅长学习社会显著信息。他引用了一项2004年的经典研究，达特茅斯学院和哈佛大学的心理学家使用功能性磁共振成像追踪17名年轻男子的大脑活动，当他们听取人物描述时，专注于社会相关线索（例如，试图根据描述形成对一个人的印象）或更社会中立的信息（如注意描述中细节的顺序）。在每种条件下描述相同，但当有社会动机时，人们能更好地记住这些陈述。

paragraphs.text: The study also found that when subjects thought about and later recalled descriptions in terms of their informational content, regions associated with factual memory, such as the medial temporal lobe, became active. But thinking about or remembering descriptions in terms of their social meaning activated the dorsomedial prefrontal cortex—part of the brain's social network—even as traditional memory regions registered low levels of activity. More recently, as he reported in a 2012 review, Lieberman has discovered that this region may be part of a distinct network involved in socially motivated learning and memory. Such findings, he says, suggest that "this network can be called on to process and store the kind of information taught in school—potentially giving students access to a range of untapped mental powers."
paragraphs.translation: 研究还发现，当受试者从信息内容角度思考和后来回忆描述时，与事实记忆相关的区域（如内侧颞叶）变得活跃。但从社会意义角度思考或记住描述时，激活了背内侧前额叶皮层——大脑社交网络的一部分——即使传统记忆区域记录的活动水平较低。最近，正如他在2012年的一篇综述中报告的，利伯曼发现这个区域可能是一个独特的网络的一部分，涉及社会动机学习和记忆。他说，这些发现表明，“这个网络可以被调动来处理和存储学校所教的信息——可能让学生获得一系列未开发的心智能力。”

paragraphs.text: If humans are generally geared to recall details about one another, this pattern is probably even more powerful among teenagers who are very attentive to social details: who is in, who is out, who likes whom, who is mad at whom. Their penchant for social drama is not—or not only—a way of distracting themselves from their schoolwork or of driving adults crazy. It is actually a neurological(神经的) sensitivity, initiated by hormonal changes. Evolutionarily speaking, people in this age group are at a stage in which they can prepare to find a mate and start their own family while separating from parents and striking out on their own. To do this successfully, their brain prompts them to think and even obsess about others.
paragraphs.translation: 如果人类通常倾向于记住关于彼此的细节，那么在青少年中，这种模式可能更加强大，因为他们非常关注社交细节：谁得势、谁失势、谁喜欢谁、谁生谁的气。他们对社交戏剧的偏好不是——或不仅仅是——分散自己对学业的注意力或让成年人抓狂的方式。实际上，这是一种由激素变化引发的神经敏感性。从进化角度讲，这个年龄段的人处于一个阶段，他们可以在与父母分离并独立生活的同时，准备寻找伴侣并组建自己的家庭。为了成功做到这一点，他们的大脑促使他们思考甚至痴迷于他人。

paragraphs.text: Yet our schools focus primarily on students as individual entities. What would happen if educators instead took advantage of the fact that teens are powerfully compelled to think in social terms? In Social, Lieberman lays out a number of ways to do so. History and English could be presented through the lens of the psychological drives of the people involved. One could therefore present Napoleon in terms of his desire to impress or Churchill in terms of his lonely melancholy. Less inherently interpersonal subjects, such as math, could acquire a social aspect through team problem solving and peer tutoring. Research shows that when we absorb information in order to teach it to someone else, we learn it more accurately and deeply, perhaps in part because we are engaging our social cognition.
paragraphs.translation: 然而，我们的学校主要关注学生作为个体。如果教育者转而利用青少年强烈被迫以社交方式思考的事实，会发生什么？在《社交》中，利伯曼提出了几种方法。历史和英语可以通过涉及人物的心理动机来呈现。因此，可以用拿破仑渴望给人留下深刻印象的角度来介绍他，或用丘吉尔孤独忧郁的角度来介绍他。天生不那么人际关系的学科，如数学，可以通过团队问题解决和同伴辅导获得社交方面。研究表明，当我们为了教别人而吸收信息时，我们学得更准确、更深入，部分原因可能是因为我们使用了社交认知。

paragraphs.text: And although anxious parents may not welcome the notion, educators could turn adolescent recklessness to academic ends. "Risk taking in an educational context is a vital skill that enables progress and creativity," wrote Sarah-Jayne Blakemore, a cognitive neuroscientist at University College London, in a review published last year. Yet, she noted, many young people are especially risk averse at school—afraid that one low test score or mediocre grade could cost them a spot at a selective university. We should assure such students that risk, and even peer pressure, can be a good thing—as long as it happens in the classroom and not the car.
paragraphs.translation: 尽管焦虑的父母可能不欢迎这个想法，但教育者可以将青少年的鲁莽转化为学术目的。伦敦大学学院的认知神经科学家萨拉-杰恩·布莱克莫尔在去年发表的一篇综述中写道：“在教育环境中，冒险是一项至关重要的技能，它能够促进进步和创造力。”然而，她指出，许多年轻人在学校特别规避风险——担心一次低分或平庸的成绩可能会让他们失去进入顶尖大学的机会。我们应该向这些学生保证，风险甚至同伴压力可以是好事——只要它发生在教室里，而不是在车里。

questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落G。段落G中提到'What our study suggests is that teenagers learn more quickly and more effectively when their peers are present than when they're on their own'（我们的研究表明，青少年在同龄人在场时比单独时学习得更快、更有效），这与陈述中的'the presence of peers increases the speed and effectiveness of teenagers' learning'（同龄人的存在增加了青少年学习的速度和效果）相匹配。

questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落F。段落F中提到'The brains of teenagers, but not adults, showed greater activity in two regions associated with rewards when they were being observed by same-age peers than when alone'（当被同龄同伴观察时，青少年的大脑在与奖励相关的两个区域显示出更大的活动，而不是成人），这与陈述中的'The presence of peer intensifies the feeling of rewards in teens' brains'（同龄人的存在加强了青少年大脑中奖励的感觉）相匹配。

questions.statementText: When we absorb information for the purpose of imparting it to others, we do so with greater secretary and depth.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落K。段落K中提到'Research shows that when we absorb information in order to teach it to someone else, we learn it more accurately and deeply'（研究表明，当我们为了教给别人而吸收信息时，我们更准确地和深入地学习它），这与陈述中的'When we absorb information for the purpose of imparting it to others, we do so with greater secretary and depth'（当我们为了传授给他人而吸收信息时，我们以更大的秘书和深度这样做）相匹配。

questions.statementText: Some experts are suggesting that we turn peer influence to good use in education.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落D。段落D中提到'Now some experts are proposing that we should take advantage of the teen brain's keen sensitivity to the presence of friends and leverage it to improve education'（现在一些专家提议我们应该利用青少年大脑对朋友存在的敏感性，并利用它来改善教育），这与陈述中的'Some experts are suggesting that we turn peer influence to good use in education'（一些专家建议我们将同伴影响用于教育中的好事）相匹配。

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: The Ebro Delta, in Spain, famous as a battleground during the Spanish Civil War, is now the setting for a different contest, one that is pitting rice farmers against two enemies: the rice-eating giant apple snail, and rising sea levels. What happens here will have a bearing on the future of European rice production and the overall health of southern European wetlands.
paragraphs.translation: 西班牙的埃布罗三角洲，曾因西班牙内战期间的战场而闻名，如今成为另一场较量的舞台，这场较量让稻农与两个敌人对抗：以稻米为食的巨型苹果螺，以及不断上升的海平面。这里发生的事情将对欧洲稻米生产的未来和南欧湿地的整体健康产生影响。

paragraphs.text: Located on the Mediterranean just two hours south of Barcelona, the Ebro Delta produces 120 million kilograms of rice a year, making it one of the continent's most important rice-growing areas. As the sea creeps into these freshwater marshes, however, rising salinity (盐分) is hampering rice production. At the same time, this sea-water also kills off the greedy giant apple snail, an introduced pest that feeds on young rice plants. The most promising strategy has become to harness one foe against the other.
paragraphs.translation: 埃布罗三角洲位于地中海沿岸，巴塞罗那以南仅两小时车程，每年生产1.2亿公斤稻米，使其成为欧洲大陆最重要的稻米种植区之一。然而，随着海水渗入这些淡水沼泽，盐度上升正在阻碍稻米生产。与此同时，海水也杀死了贪婪的巨型苹果螺，这是一种外来害虫，以幼稻为食。最有前景的策略变成了利用一个敌人对抗另一个敌人。

paragraphs.text: The battle is currently being waged on land, in greenhouses at the University of Barcelona. Scientists working under the banner "Project Neurice" are seeking varieties of rice that can withstand the increasing salinity without losing the absorbency that makes European rice ideal for traditional Spanish and Italian dishes.
paragraphs.translation: 这场战斗目前在陆地上进行，在巴塞罗那大学的温室里。在“Neurice项目”旗帜下工作的科学家们正在寻找能够耐受日益增加的盐度，同时不失去使欧洲稻米适合传统西班牙和意大利菜肴的吸收性的稻米品种。

paragraphs.text: "The project has two sides," says Xavier Serrat, Neurice project manager and researcher at the University of Barcelona. "The short-term fight against the snail, and a mid- to long-term fight against climate change. But the snail has given the project greater urgency."
paragraphs.translation: “这个项目有两面，”Neurice项目经理、巴塞罗那大学研究员Xavier Serrat说。“短期是对抗蜗牛，中长期是对抗气候变化。但蜗牛给了项目更大的紧迫性。”

paragraphs.text: Originally from South America, the snails were accidentally introduced into the Ebro Delta by Global Aquatic Technologies, a company that raised the snails for fresh-water aquariums (水族馆), but failed to prevent their escape. For now, the giant apple snail's foothold in Europe is limited to the Ebro Delta. But the snail continues its march to new territory, says Serrat. "The question is not if it will reach other rice-growing areas of Europe, but when."
paragraphs.translation: 这些蜗牛原产于南美洲，被全球水产技术公司意外引入埃布罗三角洲，该公司为淡水水族馆养殖蜗牛，但未能阻止其逃脱。目前，巨型苹果螺在欧洲的立足点仅限于埃布罗三角洲。但Serrat说，蜗牛继续向新领地进军。“问题不是它是否会到达欧洲其他稻米种植区，而是什么时候。”

paragraphs.text: Over the next year and a half investigators will test the various strains of saline-tolerant rice they've concocted. In 2018, farmers will plant the varieties with the most promise in the Ebro Delta and Europe's other two main rice-growing regions—along the Po in Italy, and France's Rhône. A season in the field will help determine which, if any, of the varieties are ready for commercialization.
paragraphs.translation: 在接下来的一年半里，研究人员将测试他们培育的各种耐盐稻米品种。2018年，农民将在埃布罗三角洲和欧洲其他两个主要稻米种植区——意大利的波河沿岸和法国的罗讷河——种植最有前景的品种。田间的一个季节将帮助确定哪些品种（如果有的话）准备好商业化。

paragraphs.text: As an EU-funded effort, the search for salt-tolerant varieties of rice is taking place in all three countries. Each team is crossbreeding a local European short-grain rice with a long-grain Asian variety that carries the salt-resistant gene. The scientists are breeding successive generations to arrive at varieties that incorporate salt tolerance but retain about 97 percent of the European rice genome (基因组).
paragraphs.translation: 作为欧盟资助的努力，对耐盐稻米品种的搜索正在所有三个国家进行。每个团队都在将本地欧洲短粒稻米与携带抗盐基因的亚洲长粒稻米进行杂交。科学家们正在培育连续几代，以获得既具有耐盐性又保留约97%欧洲稻米基因组的品种。

questionGroups.directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some question or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.questionText: Why does the author mention the Spanish Civil War at the beginning of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: It had great impact on the life of Spanish rice farmers.

options.label: B
options.text: It is of great significance in the records of Spanish history.

options.label: C
options.text: Rice farmers in the Ebro Delta are waging a battle of similar importance.

options.label: D
options.text: Rice farmers in the Ebro Delta are experiencing as hard a time as in the war.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。作者在文章开头提到西班牙内战，是为了引出现在Ebro Delta地区稻农面临的不同战斗，即与巨型苹果蜗牛和海平面上升的斗争。'one that is pitting rice farmers against two enemies'与选项C中的'Rice farmers in the Ebro Delta are waging a battle of similar importance'相对应，因此C是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 'It had great impact on the life of Spanish rice farmers'与原文无关，原文并未提及西班牙内战对稻农生活的影响。
wrongOptions.B: 'It is of great significance in the records of Spanish history'同样与原文无关，原文并未强调其在西班牙历史记录中的重要性。
wrongOptions.D: 'Rice farmers in the Ebro Delta are experiencing as hard a time as in the war'虽然提到了战争，但原文并没有直接比较当前稻农的困境与战争时期的困难程度。

questions.questionText: What may be the most effective strategy for rice farmers to employ in fighting their enemies?

options.label: B

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.text: Using one evil to combat the other.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章提到，'The most promising strategy has become to harness one foe against the other.'，即利用一个敌人对抗另一个敌人，与选项D中的'Using one evil to combat the other'相对应，因此D是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 'Striking the weaker enemy first'并未在文中提及，文章强调的是同时对抗两个敌人。
wrongOptions.B: 'Eliminating the enemy one by one'同样未提及，文章中提到的是同时利用两个敌人之间的对抗。
wrongOptions.C: 'Killing two birds with one stone'虽然意为一石二鸟，但文章中强调的是利用一个敌人对抗另一个，而不是同时消灭两个敌人。

questions.questionText: What do we learn about "Project Neurice"?

options.label: A
options.text: Its goals will have to be realized at a cost.

options.label: B
options.text: It aims to increase the yield of Spanish rice.

options.label: C

options.label: D

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章中提到，'The project has two sides,' says Xavier Serrat, Neurice project manager and researcher at the University of Barcelona. 'The short-term fight against the snail, and a mid- to long-term fight against climate change.' 说明项目的当务之急是控制害虫，与选项C中的'Its immediate priority is to bring the pest under control'相对应，因此C是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 'Its goals will have to be realized at a cost'并未在文中提及，文章没有讨论实现目标的成本问题。
wrongOptions.B: 'It aims to increase the yield of Spanish rice'虽然可能与项目的目标相关，但并非文章明确提到的项目内容。
wrongOptions.D: 'It tries to kill the snails with the help of climate change'与原文相反，文章中提到的是对抗气候变化，而不是利用气候变化。

questions.questionText: What does Neurice project manager say about the giant apple snail?

options.label: A
options.text: It can survive only on southern European wetlands.

options.label: B
options.text: It will invade other rice-growing regions of Europe.

options.label: C
options.text: It multiplies at a speed beyond human imagination.

options.label: D

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章中提到，'But the snail continues its march to new territory, says Serrat. 'The question is not if it will reach other rice-growing areas of Europe, but when.' 说明巨型苹果蜗牛将会入侵欧洲其他稻米种植区，与选项B中的'It will invade other rice-growing regions of Europe'相对应，因此B是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 'It can survive only on southern European wetlands'与原文不符，原文并未提及蜗牛只能在南欧湿地生存。
wrongOptions.C: 'It multiplies at a speed beyond human imagination'并未在文中提及，文章没有讨论蜗牛的繁殖速度。
wrongOptions.D: 'It was introduced into the rice fields on purpose'与原文相反，文章中提到蜗牛是意外引入的，并非故意。

questions.questionText: What is the ultimate goal of the EU-funded program?

options.label: A
options.text: Cultivating ideal salt-resistant rice varieties.

options.label: B
options.text: Increasing the absorbency of the Spanish rice.

options.label: C
options.text: Introducing Spanish rice to the rest of Europe.

options.label: D
options.text: Popularizing the rice crossbreeding technology.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章最后一段提到，'As an EU-funded effort, the search for salt-tolerant varieties of rice is taking place in all three countries.' 说明欧盟资助的项目旨在寻找耐盐的稻米品种，与选项A中的'Cultivating ideal salt-resistant rice varieties'相对应，因此A是正确答案。

wrongOptions.B: 'Increasing the absorbency of the Spanish rice'并未在文中提及，文章关注的是耐盐性而非吸水性。
wrongOptions.C: 'Introducing Spanish rice to the rest of Europe'与原文无关，项目的目标是培育耐盐品种，而非推广西班牙稻米。

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: Photography was once an expensive, laborious ordeal reserved for life's greatest milestones. Now, the only apparent cost to taking infinite photos of something as common as a meal is the space on your hard drive and your dining companion's patience.
paragraphs.translation: 摄影曾经是一项昂贵、费力的磨难，专为人生最重要的里程碑而设。如今，拍摄像一顿饭这样普通事物的无限照片，唯一明显的代价是硬盘空间和用餐同伴的耐心。

paragraphs.text: But is there another cost, a deeper cost, to documenting a life experience instead of simply enjoying it? "You hear that you shouldn't take all these photos and interrupt the experience, and it's bad for you, and we're not living in the present moment," says Kristin Diehl, associate professor of marketing at the University of Southern California Marshall School of Business.
paragraphs.translation: 但是，记录生活体验而不是单纯享受它，是否有另一种代价，更深层次的代价呢？“你听说不应该拍这么多照片，打断体验，这对你不好，我们没有活在当下，”南加州大学马歇尔商学院营销学副教授克里斯汀·迪尔说。

paragraphs.text: Diehl and her fellow researchers wanted to find out if that was true, so they embarked on a series of nine experiments in the lab and in the field testing people's enjoyment in the presence or absence of a camera. The results, published in the Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, surprised them. Taking photos actually makes people enjoy what they're doing more, not less.
paragraphs.translation: 迪尔和她的同事们想知道这是否属实，因此他们进行了一系列九项实验，在实验室和实地测试人们在有或没有相机的情况下享受程度。结果发表在《人格与社会心理学杂志》上，令他们惊讶。拍照实际上让人们更享受他们所做的事情，而不是减少。

paragraphs.text: "What we find is you actually look at the world slightly differently, because you're looking for things you want to capture, that you may want to hang onto," Diehl explains. "That gets people more engaged in the experience, and they tend to enjoy it more."
paragraphs.translation: “我们发现，你实际上以略微不同的方式看待世界，因为你在寻找你想捕捉的东西，那些你可能想留住的东西，”迪尔解释道。“这使人们更投入于体验，他们往往更享受它。”

paragraphs.text: Take sightseeing. In one experiment, nearly 200 participants boarded a double-decker bus for a tour of Philadelphia. Both bus tours forbade the use of cell phones but one tour provided digital cameras and encouraged people to take photos. The people who took photos enjoyed the experience significantly more, and said they were more engaged, than those who didn't.
paragraphs.translation: 以观光为例。在一项实验中，近200名参与者登上双层巴士游览费城。两次巴士游览都禁止使用手机，但一次提供了数码相机并鼓励人们拍照。拍照的人比不拍的人明显更享受这次体验，并表示他们更投入。

paragraphs.text: Snapping a photo directs attention, which heightens the pleasure you get from whatever you're looking at, Diehl says. It works for things as boring as archaeological (考古的) museums, where people were given eye-tracking glasses and instructed either to take photos or not. "People look longer at things they want to photograph," Diehl says. They report liking the exhibits more, too.
paragraphs.translation: 拍一张照片会引导注意力，从而增强你从所看事物中获得的快乐，迪尔说。这甚至适用于像考古博物馆这样无聊的事情，在那里人们被给予眼动追踪眼镜，并被指示是否拍照。“人们会更长时间地看他们想拍照的东西，”迪尔说。他们也报告更喜欢这些展品。

paragraphs.text: To the relief of Instagrammers (Instagram 用户) everywhere, it can even make meals more enjoyable. When people were encouraged to take at least three photos while they ate lunch, they were more immersed in their meals than those who weren't told to take photos.
paragraphs.translation: 让各地的Instagram用户欣慰的是，它甚至可以使用餐更愉快。当人们被鼓励在吃午餐时至少拍三张照片时，他们比没有被要求拍照的人更沉浸在用餐中。

paragraphs.text: Was it the satisfying click of the camera? The physical act of the snap? No, they found; just the act of planning to take a photo—and not actually taking it—had the same joy-boosting effect. "If you want to take mental photos, that works the same way," Diehl says. "Thinking about what you would want to photograph also gets you more engaged."
paragraphs.translation: 是相机那令人满意的咔哒声吗？还是拍快照的物理动作？不，他们发现；仅仅是计划拍照的动作——而不实际拍照——就有同样的提升快乐的效果。“如果你想拍心理照片，效果也是一样的，”迪尔说。“思考你想拍什么也能让你更投入。

questionGroups.directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some question or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). questions.questionText: What does the author say about photo-taking in the past?

options.label: A
options.text: It was a painstaking effort for recording life's major events.

options.label: B
options.text: It was a luxury that only a few wealthy people could enjoy.

options.label: C
options.text: It was a good way to preserve one's precious images.

options.label: D
options.text: It was a skill that required lots of practice to master.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。根据文章第一段'Photography was once an expensive, laborious ordeal reserved for life's greatest milestones'可以得知，过去拍照是一种费力且昂贵的活动，仅用于记录生命中的重大事件。因此，选项A 'It was a painstaking effort for recording life's major events' 是正确答案。

wrongOptions.B: 'a luxury that only a few wealthy people could enjoy' 与原文不符，原文没有提到只有富人才能享受摄影。
wrongOptions.C: 'a good way to preserve one's precious images' 与原文不符，原文强调的是摄影的昂贵和费力，而非保存图像。
wrongOptions.D: 'a skill that required lots of practice to master' 与原文不符，原文没有提到摄影需要大量练习来掌握。

questions.questionText: Kristin Diehl conducted a series of experiments on photo-taking to find out_________.

options.label: A
options.text: what kind of pleasure it would actually bring to photo-takers

options.label: B
options.text: whether people enjoyed it when they did sightseeing

options.label: C
options.text: how it could help to enrich people's life experiences

options.label: D
options.text: whether it prevented people enjoying what they were doing

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。根据文章第二段'But is there another cost, a deeper cost, to documenting a life experience instead of simply enjoying it?'和'Diehl and her fellow researchers wanted to find out if that was true'可以得知，Kristin Diehl 进行一系列实验是为了探究拍照是否会阻止人们享受他们正在做的事情。因此，选项D 'whether it prevented people enjoying what they were doing' 是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 'what kind of pleasure it would actually bring to photo-takers' 与原文不符，原文关注的是拍照是否会减少人们的享受，而非带来快乐。
wrongOptions.B: 'whether people enjoyed it when they did sightseeing' 只是实验的一部分，不是实验的总体目的。
wrongOptions.C: 'how it could help to enrich people's life experiences' 与实验目的相反，实验是为了探究拍照是否会减少人们的享受。

questions.questionText: What do the results of Diehl's experiments show about people taking pictures?

options.label: A
options.text: They are distracted from what they are doing.

options.label: B
options.text: They can better remember what they see or do.

options.label: C
options.text: They are more absorbed in what catches their eye.

options.label: D
options.text: They can have a better understanding of the world.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。根据文章第三段'Taking photos actually makes people enjoy what they're doing more, not less'和'That gets people more engaged in the experience, and they tend to enjoy it more'可以得知，拍照使人们更加专注于他们所做的事情，并且更加享受。因此，选项C 'They are more absorbed in what catches their eye' 是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 'They are distracted from what they are doing' 与原文不符，原文指出拍照使人们更加专注和享受。
wrongOptions.B: 'They can better remember what they see or do' 原文没有提到拍照能帮助人们更好地记住他们看到或做的事情。
wrongOptions.D: 'They can have a better understanding of the world' 与原文不符，原文没有提到拍照能帮助人们更好地理解世界。

questions.questionText: What is found about museum visitors with the aid of eye-tracking glasses?

options.label: A
options.text: They come out with better photographs of the exhibits.

options.label: B
options.text: They focus more on the exhibits when taking pictures.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。根据文章第五段'People look longer at things they want to photograph'和'They report liking the exhibits more, too'可以得知，使用眼动追踪眼镜的博物馆参观者在拍照时更加关注展品。因此，选项B 'They focus more on the exhibits when taking pictures' 是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 'They come out with better photographs of the exhibits' 与原文不符，原文没有提到照片的质量。
wrongOptions.C: 'They have a better view of what are on display' 与原文不符，原文没有提到参观者的视野更好。

questions.questionText: What do we learn from the last paragraph?

options.label: A
options.text: It is better to make plans before taking photos.

options.label: B
options.text: Mental photos can be as beautiful as snapshots.

options.label: C
options.text: Photographers can derive great joy from the click of the camera.

options.label: D
options.text: Even the very thought of taking a photo can have a positive effect.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。根据文章最后一段'just the act of planning to take a photo—and not actually taking it—had the same joy-boosting effect'可以得知，即使是拍照的想法也能产生积极的效果。因此，选项D 'Even the very thought of taking a photo can have a positive effect' 是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 'It is better to make plans before taking photos' 与原文不符，原文没有提到拍照前制定计划更好。
wrongOptions.B: 'Mental photos can be as beautiful as snapshots' 与原文不符，原文没有提到心理照片和快照一样美丽。
wrongOptions.C: 'Photographers can derive great joy from the click of the camera' 与原文不符，原文没有提到摄影师可以从相机的点击声中获得巨大快乐。

questionGroups.sourceText: 过去，拥有一辆私家车对大部分中国人而言是件奢侈的事。如今，私家车在中国随处可见。汽车成了人们生活中不可或缺的一部分，他们不仅开车上下班，还经常驾车出游。有些城市的汽车增长速度过快，以至于交通拥堵和停车位不足的问题日益严峻，这些城市的市政府不得不出台新规，限制上路汽车的数量。由于空气污染日益严重，现在越来越多的人选择购买新能源汽车，中国政府也采取了一些措施，支持新能源汽车的发展。

answer.modelTranslation: In the past, owning a private car was a luxury for most Chinese people. Nowadays, private cars are ubiquitous in China. Cars have become an indispensable part of people's lives; they not only drive to work and back but also often go on road trips. In some cities, the rapid growth of cars has led to increasingly severe issues of traffic congestion and insufficient parking spaces, forcing municipal governments to introduce new regulations to limit the number of cars on the road. Due to the worsening air pollution, more and more people are choosing to buy new energy vehicles, and the Chinese government has also taken some measures to support the development of new energy vehicles.
